item.description: An array of imports are subject to the new 50 percent tariffs. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has called them “a miscalculation” and vowed to match them “dollar for dollar.”

item.title: Canada's leader announces retaliatory tariffs against U.S. after potential trade deal collapses
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney, referring to President Donald Trump's new 50 percent tariffs that went into effect early Saturday as as "a miscalculation," said the Canadian levies on U.S. goods will take effect Sept. 8.

item.title: ICE begins deporting Haitians who recently lost temporary protected status back to homeland
item.description: Community leaders said a removal flight on Thursday carried 170 people ranging in age from 19 to 71 and included people who were detained in recent weeks. The U.S. Supreme Court cleared the way for the Trump administration to end humanitarian protections for Haitians in June.

item.title: Progressive Aisha Wahab wins House runoff to replace Eric Swalwell in California contest shaped by pro-Israel group’s spending
item.description: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee’s super PAC poured nearly $2.5 million into the race in a bid to boost Wahab’s opponent, fellow Democrat Melissa Hernandez. Wahab, a state senator, will serve the rest of Swalwell’s term after he resigned amid a sexual assault allegation.

item.title: Pentagon’s shakeup at Stars and Stripes risks eroding independence of military newspaper, Democrats say
item.description: The longtime Stars and Stripes publisher announced he was stepping away in an email to staff that included a parting shot at the Defense Department. Weeks earlier, an active-duty Navy captain was placed in leadership at the military newspaper, an atypical appointment that staffers, board members and Democratic lawmakers say risks further eroding the publication’s independence from the government.
